content.title: Background Anomaly | Audience Notices, Recording Confirms
content.summary: Place an anomaly in the background while foreground routine continues. Use a recording device to isolate it as evidence, then delay the character's reaction until the anomaly changes or leaves the recorded field.

quick_start.input_format: The background anomaly appears first + the foreground remains normal + recording equipment forensics + evidence field changes + delayed response
quick_start.recommended_input: When a single greenhouse engineer calibrated the valve, non-human-shaped frost patterns appeared on the pressure window in the distance; the wall-mounted mechanical observation mirror was fixed to collect evidence, and the frost patterns migrated along the copper pipe before the figure turned around.
required_anchors: Reveal the anomaly to the viewer before the subjects notice it.
Keep foreground behavior ordinary during the first anomaly state.
Change the anomaly inside or against the evidence field.
Delay the human reaction until after the proof changes.
usage_steps: Replace the example subject, setting, and surface details with an original concept.
Keep every required anchor and Creative DNA invariant causally visible.
Choose the MiniMax H3 or Seedance 2.0 prompt and fill only the declared variable slots.
Check duration, event order, camera continuity, sound, and anti-copy constraints before generation.
applicable_scope: Place an anomaly in the background while foreground routine continues. Use a recording device to isolate it as evidence, then delay the character's reaction until the anomaly changes or leaves the recorded field.
Original 4–15 second concepts that can preserve every required anchor.
MiniMax H3 or Seedance 2.0 projects that need a reusable causal video structure.
not_suitable_for: Requests that copy the source identity, setting, props, dialogue, or shot order.
Concepts that cannot show all required anchors inside the target duration.
Long-form exposition or unrelated multi-location stories without a compact causal chain.

creative_dna.mechanism: Place an anomaly in the background before foreground subjects notice it, preserve ordinary foreground behavior, use a recording or inspection device to isolate the anomaly as evidence, let the anomaly visibly disrupt or leave that evidence field, then delay the subjects' reaction until after the proof changes.

invariants.rule: Reveal the anomaly to the viewer before the subjects notice it.
Keep foreground behavior ordinary during the first anomaly state.
Use one device or inspection frame to isolate the anomaly.
invariants.ablation_failure: A random close-up does not prove discovery.

invariants.rule: Change the anomaly inside or against the evidence field.
invariants.purpose: Makes the proof active rather than static.
invariants.ablation_failure: An unchanged recording adds no causal turn.

invariants.rule: Delay the human reaction until after the proof changes.

slots.name: lead_subject
slots.constraint: An original stable subject or pair whose role is clear without source identity.

slots.name: setting
slots.constraint: A materially new setting with fixed spatial anchors and no source-specific location.

slots.name: causal_carrier
slots.constraint: One object, route, mark or device that visibly carries the causal chain.

slots.name: state_change
slots.constraint: Five ordered states with observable handoffs, not a decorative montage.

slots.name: camera_grammar
slots.constraint: A new proof-oriented information order that does not copy source shot boundaries.

slots.name: payoff
slots.constraint: A held final consequence that resolves or recontextualizes the setup.

slots.name: sound_family
slots.constraint: An original hierarchy of story-world cues supporting each visible change.

anti_copy_exclusions: source anime women and neon alley
purple ghost silhouette and smartphone screen
